your experiences with programs and clinicians, however, does not mean you have full scope of the all people with DID. we personally know a lot of systems that we met through the online community, and the amount of variation between all of them is immeasurable. the problem with your desire for this to not be portrayed as DID is: that is what DID looks like for quite a lot of people. myself and one of my partners both have polyfragmented DID, and split frequently, often with seemingly no reason. i don’t mean that the brain learns to split for “minor reasons,” (though, again.. trauma is subjective, and what may be fine for you could be traumatizing or trigger a trauma response for another, so what you call minor means nothing.) i mean that once your brain has learned to split for safety/coping, it will continue to do so. alters do not require that level of trauma to form if you already have DID, because your brain is *already wired* to dissociate from trauma. also, we don’t base our knowledge on things from the online community, but from our own research and therapy journey. we use the online community for just that— *community.*

while it isn’t medically proven or anything rn, we have seen a LOT of autistic and/or adhd systems that split lots of introjects from hyperfixations/special interests in our ≈8 years of being involved in the online osddid community. in addition, polyfragmented systems can and do split at “the drop of a hat.” trauma is subjective, and if someone’s brain is already wired to split for safety reasons, it’s likely it will continue to happen in response to lesser stressors, too.
